items.body: Euclidean Spin(4) is decomposed into two chiral SU(2) factors in the Euclidean-first proposal.
Twistor space is C^4 / projective CP^3 with an SU(2,2) real form giving positive, negative, and null/boundary orbits for the Minkowski picture.
W04e proposes a new conjugation-like structure interchanging positive/negative imaginary-time sectors while preserving a Lorentzian-chiral subspace.
W01 fixes the Euclidean vector real form inside M(2,C) by the Pauli-matrix map, with determinant equal to positive Euclidean norm squared and an equivalent quaternion presentation with x KAPPA(x).
W01 represents Spin(4) by independent left/right SU(2)=Sp(1) actions, with the Euclidean vector action x -> g_L x g_R^{-1}; the two factors are structurally independent in Euclidean signature.

W01 identifies the common complexification of Euclidean, Minkowski, and split-signature four-vector spaces with M(2,C)=Hom(S_R,S_L), while retaining different real-form/action constraints for each signature.

W01's frame-bundle description distinguishes spin-connection one-forms omega from canonical/frame one-forms e, takes e and omega as the fundamental Palatini fields, and writes the action as the integral of epsilon_ABCD e^A wedge e^B wedge Omega^CD(omega); its equations of motion are obtained by varying omega^AB, which gives de^A + omega^A_B wedge e^B = 0 and thereby the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection determined by e, and by varying e^A, which gives the Einstein equations in terms of e.
W01 decomposes spin connection, curvature, and two-forms into chiral/Hodge sectors; the right and left connection-curvature pairs act on S_R and S_L respectively.

For a torsion-free connection W01 states the vacuum Einstein condition as vanishing of a specified mixed/chiral curvature component and motivates a chiral formulation using only the right-handed connection/curvature sector; the omitted left connection becomes unconstrained if torsion is allowed.

W01 constructs the weak SU(2)_L gauge sector from the left spin connection and uses the imaginary-time component of the canonical one-form as a Higgs candidate; it explicitly records the missing electroweak U(1) and SU(2)_R-invariance problems that motivate the twistor-space reformulation.
W01 identifies Euclidean projective twistor space CP3 -> S4 as the bundle whose CP1/S2 fiber parametrizes orthogonal complex structures J on each R4 tangent space, with J^2=-1.

For a chosen orthogonal complex structure J, W01 decomposes R4 tensor C into +i/-i eigenspaces and constructs S_R and S_L through exterior powers; the stabilizer U(2) lifts to SU(2)_L x U(1) with U(1) inside SU(2)_R.
On PT the lifted spinor roles have U(1) weights S_L=C^2_0 and S_R=C_-1 + C_+1 under SU(2)_L x U(1).

W01 defines the tautological line L over PT and the rank-3 quotient L^perp=C4/L; PT is SU(4)/S(U(1)xU(3)), SU(3) acts on L^perp as the color group, and the determinant-one condition fixes the relative U(1) weights.

W01 represents one Standard Model generation by Hom(l + l^perp, S_R + S_L), whose SU(3)xSU(2)_LxU(1) decomposition reproduces the listed quark/lepton transformation roles including a right-handed neutrino.
In W01 the U(1) and SU(3) gauge principal bundles are intrinsic to PT rather than pullbacks from S4; a full interacting theory on PT is explicitly left undeveloped.

W01 identifies the t=0 compactified Minkowski S3 with the equator of Euclidean S4 and the null PT_0 locus Phi(s,s)=0; upper/lower Euclidean hemispheres correspond to positive/negative imaginary-time regions.
For free massless spinors W01 uses the Penrose transform H^1(PT_+,O(-3)) <-> Weyl solutions on S4_+ and fiber restriction H^1(CP1,O(-3))=C2 to reconstruct pointwise spinor values.

W01 states the Penrose-Ward correspondence between anti-self-dual gauge connections on spacetime regions and holomorphic vector bundles on twistor regions, with the explicit limitation that this directly covers anti-self-dual rather than general Yang-Mills fields.

W01 requires any future PT quantum theory to relate fields on the five-dimensional PT_0 fibered over S3 to ordinary state data on S3 and notes that the intrinsic PT gauge bundles vary along CP1 fibers, so ordinary pullback correspondence is insufficient.

Appendix A identifies compactified complex spacetime with G_2,4(C), its tautological rank-2 bundle S and quotient S^perp, and tangent bundle TM=Hom(S,S^perp); the Klein relation omega wedge omega=0 embeds the Grassmannian into projective Lambda^2(C4).
Appendix A defines the line-plane incidence relation s^perp=Zs and the fractional-linear SL(4,C) action Z -> (C+DZ)(A+BZ)^-1; the correspondence space P(S) links PT and M.
Appendix A defines alpha-planes from a twistor point and states that two spacetime points incident with the same projective twistor have null separation in the determinant quadratic form.
Appendix A distinguishes the Penrose transform for massless helicity equations from the Penrose-Ward extension with gauge fields, including open-set and fiber-triviality side conditions.

Appendix A distinguishes split, Minkowski, Euclidean, and compact SU(4) real-form structures of SL(4,C), each with different fixed/orbit/signature conditions; these real forms may not be collapsed into one representation.
For Minkowski twistor geometry W01 uses a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form Phi, anti-Hermitian affine coordinates, the SU(2,2) orbit decomposition of M/PT, and conjugate-dual left/right spinor actions.

For Euclidean twistor geometry W01 uses T=H^2, the pseudoreal map sigma with sigma^2=-1 on T and +1 projectively, HP1 homogeneous coordinates, SL(2,H) fractional-linear action, and the CP1 fibration whose sigma action is antipodal on each fiber.

Appendix B treats reconstruction of physical states from Euclidean data as requiring a chosen imaginary-time half-space/reflection and states that the resulting distinction between positive and negative imaginary time breaks SO(4) despite SO(4)-invariant Schwinger functions.

Appendix B gives the single-Weyl-field obstruction: a one-chirality Euclidean path-integral/Lagrangian cannot be made SO(4)-invariant in the conventional construction without opposite chirality/doubling; this motivates the source's alternative interpretation.

Appendix C treats Wightman/distribution data as boundary-value/hyperfunction structure and makes positive/negative holomorphic-domain decomposition load-bearing to the source's analytic-continuation discussion.

W04a writes a right-handed Minkowski Weyl equation of the form (E-sigma dot p) psi_R=0, derives the Klein-Gordon mass-shell consequence, and associates its positive- and negative-energy branches with opposite helicities.

W04a contrasts the right-handed Minkowski Wightman kernel with the naive Euclidean substitution and makes the failure of a one-chirality Euclidean propagator/Lagrangian a concrete Wick-rotation obstruction.

In the conventional four-dimensional spinor-vector description W04a represents a complex vector as a map from the dual right spinor to the left spinor; Minkowski reality relates the two chiralities by conjugation whereas Euclidean signature leaves them independent.
In the CP1 analogue W04b uses the three SU(1,1)=SL(2,R) orbits and hyperfunction boundary values to model the relation between holomorphic domains and Lorentzian boundary data.
In four dimensions W04b uses the SU(2,2)=Spin(4,2) action on PT with positive, negative, and null orbits; compactified Minkowski points are represented by CP1s contained in the null orbit.

For the Euclidean real form W04b uses SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1), C4=H2, and the CP3 -> HP1=S4 fibration with CP1 fibers; Wick rotation requires choosing such a Euclidean fibration and its intersection with the Minkowski null geometry.

W04d identifies the spectral positivity of time evolution with holomorphy of U(z)=exp(-izH) in a complex-time half-plane and treats this holomorphic-domain structure as the operational core of Wick rotation.

W04e instead uses an antilinear reflection/conjugation Theta associated with imaginary-time reflection in Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction; the Hilbert-space inner product and physical state space are reconstructed from this reflection-positive Euclidean structure.

The W04e reconstruction requires choosing an imaginary-time half-space/direction and reflection, so the physical-state reconstruction breaks Euclidean SO(4) even when the underlying Euclidean correlation data are SO(4)-covariant.

In the twistor version W04e uses a Hermitian form Phi to split projective twistor space into positive, negative, and null regions; holomorphic theory on PT+ is proposed to have boundary values on the null region representing chiral Minkowski data, with Penrose/Penrose-Ward constructions supplying part of the reconstruction machinery.

W04d explicitly contrasts the conventional complex vector carrier S_L tensor S_R with the proposed right-handed carrier S_R tensor conjugate(S_R); on the Euclidean slice the latter decomposes as a scalar plus a three-vector and SU(2)_L acts trivially.

W04d identifies conformally compactified complex spacetime with Gr(2,4,C), a spacetime point with a right-handed C2 plane in T=C4, and projective twistor space with CP3 containing the corresponding CP1.
W04d lists SU(4), SL(4,R), SL(2,H), and SU(2,2) as real forms of SL(4,C)=Spin(6,C), with the SL(2,H) and SU(2,2) forms assigned Euclidean and Minkowski geometric roles respectively.

Under the SU(2,2) real form W04d defines PT+, PT-, and PT0 by the sign of a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form; compactified Minkowski points are CP1s lying in PT0, and PT0 is the space of Minkowski light rays/celestial spheres.
Under the Euclidean SL(2,H) real form W04d uses T=C4=H2 and the CP3->HP1=S4 fibration sending each complex line to the quaternionic line it generates.

W04d gives two equivalent geometric roles for Euclidean PT: the projective right-spin bundle and the bundle of orthogonal complex structures on S4; it states that the latter construction extends to four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds and becomes a complex twistor space for anti-self-dual metrics.

W05 distinguishes ordinary conjugation on CP1 from the twistor antipodal real structure rho_tw; on the C2 coordinate carrier rho_tw squared equals -1, while on projective points applying rho_tw twice returns the same projective point and rho_tw has no projective fixed points; it also presents the same real form as a real projective conic with complex but no real points.

W05 derives rho_tw from the chosen H=C2 presentation by left multiplication by quaternion j and uses the same quaternionic mechanism on C4=H2 to define the Euclidean projective-twistor real structure.
W05 states that rho_tw on CP3 has no fixed projective points but has a four-real-dimensional family of invariant CP1 real lines parametrized by HP1=S4; each such line is a twistor P1.

W05 contrasts Euclidean and Minkowski reality: the Euclidean twistor real structure acts on PT itself and preserves the CP1 fibers, while the Minkowski reality structure naturally maps PT to its dual and interchanges spinor chirality.

W05 gives the noncompact Euclidean twistor space R4 x CP1 the complex structure determined fiberwise by the selected orthogonal complex structure and identifies the holomorphic fibration with O(1) direct-sum O(1); for quaternionic dimension d this becomes 2d copies of O(1).

W05 records the hyperkahler generalization as a sphere aI+bJ+cK of compatible complex/Kahler structures and relates the corresponding twistor spaces to hyperkahler quotients and moduli spaces generated from self-dual Yang-Mills and its dimensional reductions.

W05 presents Simpson's twistor-structure description of a pure real Hodge structure as a U(1)-equivariant holomorphic bundle on the twistor P1, with bundle degree/slope and the U(1) weights encoding the Hodge filtration.

W05 presents the non-abelian Hodge example in which the hyperkahler moduli space is viewed over CP1 through lambda-connections, with lambda=1 giving ordinary flat connections and lambda=0 giving Higgs bundles.

W05 generalizes the real quaternion algebra to quaternion algebras (a,b/F), distinguishes split and division classes by the Hilbert symbol, and notes that the real split and quaternion classes become isomorphic after complex scalar extension.

W05 associates quaternion-algebra classes with projective conics and uses the no-F-rational-point/fixed-point-free Galois action as the finite-prime analogue of the twistor P1 antipodal real structure.
W05 relates these classes to the Brauer group and Galois cohomology and records the graded Brauer-Wall/real-Clifford Z/8 periodicity as another quaternion/Clifford manifestation.

W05 reviews canonical quantization through the Heisenberg and Weil representations and states that, for a quaternion-algebra quadratic carrier, the Brauer class controls whether the associated Weil representation is true or only projective; it connects the global adelic construction to Hilbert reciprocity.

W01's Hamiltonian chiral-gravity discussion identifies the Euclidean Ashtekar canonical variables with an SU(2)-connection/canonical-form pair analogous to Yang-Mills, with a Gauss constraint plus three spatial-diffeomorphism constraints and a Hamiltonian/time-translation constraint that vanishes in the boundary-free case.

On PT, W01 uses the tautological complex line l to define the extra electroweak U(1), represents lifted tangent vectors as Hom_C(l,S_L), and states that the Higgs-direction vector transforms under U(1)×SU(2)_L; a nonzero Higgs selects the U(1) subgroup that leaves it invariant, identified with electromagnetism.

W01's speculative Clifford lift distinguishes its proposed PT construction from conventional Kogut-Susskind multiplicity: the suggested lift would give sixteen Weyl-spinor copies whose Weyl degree of freedom comes from the CP1 fiber rather than from the exterior/Clifford algebra itself.

W01 notes that anti-self-duality can be written as a moment-map zero condition and speculates about relations to twisted N=2/N=4 Yang-Mills and geometric Langlands; these are clues, not adopted dynamics of the proposal.
W02 fixes the exact Euclidean Yang-Mills normalization used in the self-dual rewrite: (1/4g^2)∫Tr(F∧*F) differs from (1/2g^2)∫Tr(F^+∧*F^+) by the topological ∫Tr(F∧F) term.

W02 explicitly distinguishes a generic internal gauge principal bundle from the orthonormal/spin frame bundle: the latter's structure group is determined by spacetime geometry and carries the additional canonical/tetrad one-form theta absent from a generic internal gauge bundle.

W04e defines Osterwalder-Schrader conjugation on imaginary-time test functions by Theta f(tau)=conjugate(f(-tau)), with Theta an antilinear involution, and defines the OS Hermitian form by <f,g>_OS=S2(Theta f,g).

In the free-field example W04e reconstructs the physical one-particle Hilbert space as positive-time test functions modulo the null space of the OS form, and emphasizes that Theta selects an imaginary-time direction, converting SO(4) covariance into Lorentzian SO(3,1) covariance at physical-state reconstruction.

In the two-dimensional chiral model W04e distinguishes the ordinary Euclidean real form, embedded anti-diagonally in the two-chirality complexification, from a purely right-chiral holomorphic Euclidean theory; the corresponding chiral Minkowski theory is selected by a conjugation whose fixed locus is the Minkowski circle rather than by analytic continuation through the two-chirality complexification.

In four dimensions W04e places chiral SU(2,2) representations in H^1(PT+,O(n-2)) and says an appropriate twistor-transform version of Theta supplies the required conjugation/reality structure for the holomorphic PT+ theory.

W04e states that the Ward-Penrose transform gives, for suitable holomorphic bundles on PT+, right-handed Weyl solutions coupled to a self-dual connection both on a Euclidean S4 hemisphere and as boundary values on Minkowski spacetime.

W02 begins from the conventional Hermitian 2x2 complex-matrix realization of Minkowski vectors, with determinant equal to minus Minkowski length-squared and Lorentz action x -> Omega_L x Omega_R^{-1}.

Complexifying the coordinates yields a complex spacetime acted on by SL(2,C)_L x SL(2,C)_R; the real Lorentz group and Euclidean SU(2)_L x SU(2)_R rotation group occur as distinct real forms used in the conventional analytic-continuation picture.

The conventional complex-spacetime vector representation is chirally symmetric: matrices are linear maps from the dual of the right spinor to the left spinor, equivalently the (1/2)_L tensor (1/2)_R representation.

W02 distinguishes the standard twistor construction, where a point is a right-handed C2 subspace of C4 and left-handed spinors are the quotient, from its stronger proposal that the tangent bundle itself be chirally asymmetric and purely right-handed.
On the Euclidean real subspace of the right-handed construction, SU(2)_L acts trivially and SU(2)_R acts nontrivially; the right spinor and its conjugate become equivalent SU(2)_R representations.

Euclidean spacetime in the right-handed construction is a real subspace of the right-spinor tensor its conjugate, decomposing into an SU(2)_R scalar plus vector; this produces one SU(2)_R-invariant distinguished direction and a complementary three-dimensional vector subspace.

Under the conventional Euclidean vector-spinor identification, a distinguished nonzero Euclidean vector supplies an isomorphism between the left spinor and the conjugate right spinor, permitting translation between chirally symmetric and asymmetric descriptions.

For a right-handed Minkowski Weyl degree of freedom, W02 gives the momentum-space invariant Lagrangian and associates positive-energy solutions with helicity +1/2 and negative-energy solutions with helicity -1/2.

The W02 Euclidean Dirac operator uses the same 2x2 vector-matrix identification as the spacetime construction and may be interpreted purely right-handed or conventionally after a distinguished Euclidean vector identifies the two Euclidean chiral spinor spaces.

In Euclidean signature W02 uses Hodge star squared equal to +1 to split two-forms into self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors; self-dual two-forms correspond to su(2)_R and anti-self-dual two-forms to su(2)_L. In Minkowski signature star squared is -1 and the corresponding chiral decomposition requires complexification.
Complexified self-dual two-forms are identified with sl(2,C)_R, equivalently traceless endomorphisms of the right spinor and the symmetric square of two right spinors.
W02 rewrites the Euclidean Yang-Mills action, up to the topological integral of Tr(F wedge F), using only the self-dual curvature component, and therefore only right-handed spacetime spinor geometry.
W02 describes chiral general relativity using frame-bundle/spin-bundle variables: a tetrad one-form, spin connection, curvature two-form, and the self-dual/anti-self-dual decomposition of two-forms.

In the chiral GR description cited by W02, curvature acts on the six-dimensional two-form space split into two three-dimensional chiral sectors, and the Einstein equations correspond to vanishing of the off-diagonal curvature blocks.

W02 writes a chiral gravitational action as the integral of Sigma^(dotA dotB) wedge R_(dotA dotB), where Sigma is a self-dual two-form constructed from the tetrad and R is the right-handed curvature two-form; varying this action with respect to the connection gives the torsion-free (Levi-Civita) relation between the tetrad and the connection, while varying it with respect to the tetrad gives the Einstein equations.
One Standard Model fermion generation written as 32 complex components can be converted to a 64-real carrier with the same gauge action.
That 64-real carrier is identified with a positive-chiral real Majorana-Weyl Spin(11,3) spinor representation.
The Spin(11,3) GraviGUT structure embeds into Spin(12,4) and then the quaternionic real form E8(-24).
L06 explicitly keeps unresolved phenomenological/dynamical issues and does not claim the model complete.
The 2024 formulation represents C, P, T as discrete operations on fermion states and extends them with order-three triality between generations.
L05 constructs chiral Clifford basis matrices from division/split-composition algebra multiplication tables.
L05 identifies a common coefficient structure for vectors, negative-chiral spinors, positive-chiral spinors, and three division-algebra elements.
L05 defines a cyclic trilinear triality form and also permits the division-algebra product to be recovered from the triality form.
L05 uses generalized reflections and triality automorphisms to move among vector/spinor roles.

L01 places gauge fields, gravitational spin connection, frame, Higgs multiplet, and Grassmann-valued fermions over a four-dimensional base manifold, with different form degree/statistics/representation roles.

L01 combines bosonic Lie-algebra-valued 1-forms and fermionic Lie-algebra-valued Grassmann fields into one BRST-extended/superconnection A with fixed coefficients on the spin-connection and frame-Higgs terms.
L01 defines curvature by F=dA+1/2[A,A] and uses Lie brackets both as algebraic interaction structure and, in selected exceptional embeddings, as the source of subgroup-representation actions.

L01 defines Cartan subalgebra, root vectors, weights, and Cartan-Weyl decomposition; root addition corresponds to nonzero Lie brackets and particle interaction incidence, while weight coordinates are interpreted as particle quantum numbers.

L01 embeds su(3) together with defining 3 and dual bar3 weight carriers into g2=g2 decomposition su(3)+3+bar3, treating quark/anti-quark generators as Lie-algebra root vectors rather than only external representation vectors.
L01 represents gravitational so(3,1)=Cl^2(3,1) using explicit chiral Clifford matrices, decomposes the spin connection into left/right chiral blocks, and represents the frame in Cl^1(3,1).
L01 represents electroweak structure through a second Clifford/D2 sector, combines the frame with a Higgs vector, and joins gravitational/electroweak weights into a graviweak D4/so(7,1) structure.
L01 builds explicit Cl(7,1) generators and the graviweak connection H1=1/2 omega+1/4 e phi+w_ew, acting chirally on an 8-dimensional positive-chiral spinor carrier.
L01 introduces a canonical order-three D4 triality rotation cycling 8_S+, 8_S-, and 8_V and tentatively uses the three triality-related 8-dimensional roles for the three fermion generations.
L01 embeds the graviweak D4 material into F4 and represents graviweak particle interactions by root addition/Lie brackets inside that exceptional algebra.
L01 combines F4 and G2+U(1) quantum-number structures so that 222 gravitational/Standard-Model field weights match 222 of the 240 E8 roots before the remaining roots are assigned to new fields.

The E8 construction introduces an additional quantum number w and new w and xPhi field sectors; F4 is used as the centralizer of G2 in E8 and the chosen Cartan coordinates are related by explicit rotations.

L01 decomposes the E8 connection into two bosonic sectors H1 and H2 plus three fermionic generation sectors Psi_I, Psi_II, Psi_III associated with triality-related 8-dimensional roles and color/lepton factors.
L01 expands the unified curvature into F1, F2, and covariant derivatives of the three fermion sectors, retaining the E8-valued 2-form/Grassmann-form grading.

Within F1, L01 decomposes curvature into gravitational, mixed graviweak, and electroweak parts; the gravitational term combines Riemann curvature with an e e phi^2 term, while the mixed term is torsion times phi minus e Dphi.
Within F2, L01 decomposes curvature into w, B2, x, and strong su(3) parts plus an xPhi xPhi contribution, and defines the mixed x-sector through covariant derivatives of x and Phi.

L01 gives the fermionic curvature as a covariant massive Dirac derivative whose left and right algebra actions include spin, frame-Higgs, electroweak, new-field, and color terms; the other generations are asserted to have analogous curvature pieces.

L01 chooses a modified BF action with E8-valued bosonic and anti-Grassmann Lagrange-multiplier fields; eliminating the bosonic multiplier yields gravitational, fermionic, and non-gravitational gauge/action terms.

The gravitational action is reduced through the MacDowell-Mansouri-style curvature to Palatini/Einstein-Hilbert form plus cosmological constant, with Higgs magnitude acting as a conformal factor for the frame.
L01 states that the Hodge-star construction requires extracting and inverting the frame part of the E8 connection and calls this procedure awkward and in need of a more natural justification.

L01 summarizes the action as chosen by hand to agree with known Standard Model/gravity dynamics, gives high-energy coupling relations and Higgs-VEV relations for cosmological constant/masses, and claims no free parameters at that level.
L02 treats the fundamental bosonic variable as a connection H over a four-dimensional base, valued in g=spin(1+N,3), with spacetime spin(1,3), Yang-Mills spin(N), and off-diagonal complement roles.

L02 begins from a fully g-invariant polynomial extended-Plebanski action S(H,B,Phi) with one parameter g, curvature F=dH+1/2[H,H], an auxiliary g-valued 2-form B, and a symmetric operator Phi acting on bivectors and 2-forms.

Variation of H, B, and Phi gives three coupled field equations; the chosen cubic Phi potential is one convenient symmetry-breaking potential rather than a unique source requirement, and more general U(Phi) is explicitly allowed.
The symmetry-breaking construction distinguishes spin(1,3) and uses both spacetime Hodge duality and Lie-algebra bivector duality; the Hodge operator presupposes a nondegenerate gravitational frame.

L02 makes a Phi ansatz as a linear combination of identity, Hodge dual, Lie-algebra dual, and their composition; one solution class reduces to Phi=* and B=3/4 *F, leaving a Yang-Mills-form equation D*F=0.

After symmetry breaking L02 decomposes H=1/2 omega+1/4 E+A into spin connection, off-diagonal frame-Higgs, and Yang-Mills connection, and makes the simple-bivector ansatz E=e' phi with frame e' and Higgs zero-form phi.
L02 explicitly distinguishes the frame e used to build the Hodge star from the frame e' appearing in the connection and only later restricts to the solution subset e'=e.
The broken curvature decomposes into gravitational R-1/8 Sigma' phi^2, mixed T phi-e'Dphi, and Yang-Mills F_A sectors, with torsion and Higgs covariant derivative separately defined.

The symmetry-broken field equations separate into spacetime, off-diagonal, and Yang-Mills roles and admit a broad solution space; matching e'=e and setting torsion to zero (without fermionic sources) are consistent restrictions, not consequences of symmetry breaking.

Within the restricted sector L02 derives an Einstein-type equation coupled to Higgs terms but explicitly notes the resulting gravity is modified because the full field-equation set still imposes additional curvature dynamics.
With Phi=* the action becomes a Yang-Mills-form curvature-squared action; substituting the broken connection yields gravitational, torsion/Higgs, and Yang-Mills terms before further restriction.

After e'=e and vanishing torsion, the low-energy action contains Einstein-Hilbert, cosmological/Higgs potential, a Stephenson-Kilmister-Yang curvature-squared modification, Higgs kinetic, and Yang-Mills terms.

L02 gives Newton, cosmological, and Yang-Mills couplings as functions of the single initial parameter g and Higgs vacuum magnitude v, with a de Sitter/Higgs nonzero-vev background solving the restricted equations and strictly minimizing the selected action.

L02 explicitly notes the bare coupling relations are far from observed low-energy values and treats possible high-energy/fixed-point running as a qualification rather than a demonstrated phenomenological success.
Fermions couple through the covariant Dirac derivative (d+H)psi; after breaking this yields spin, frame-Higgs, and Yang-Mills interactions, and the source expects fermions to source torsion.

For a Standard-Model embedding L02 records the algebra chain SM subset Pati-Salam subset spin(10), leading in the unified setting to spin(11,3), with one generation in a 32-complex/64-real positive-chiral spinor and Higgs vev supplying Dirac masses.

L02's conclusion explicitly reconstructs the claimed physics only inside the sector satisfying the Phi ansatz, simple frame-Higgs ansatz, matched frames, and vanishing-torsion restriction; the latter two do not necessarily follow from symmetry breaking.

L03 distinguishes the conventional complex 32-component one-generation fermion representation from an exactly action-equivalent 64-real representation obtained by replacing each scalar i by a fixed real 2x2 square-minus-one matrix and each complex component by its real/imaginary pair.

The 18 gravity+Standard-Model generators in the 64-real realization retain real Lie-algebra structure constants and act on the 64-real fermion column exactly as their 32-complex counterparts act on the original generation.

L03 constructs fourteen explicit real 128x128 Cl(11,3) vector matrices whose bivectors split into positive/negative 64-real chiral blocks and whose positive block acts on a Majorana-Weyl 64-real spinor.

The 18 conventional gravity+Standard-Model 64-real generators are numerically identical, in the chosen representation, to specified positive-chiral spin(11,3) bivector combinations, making the fermion 64-real carrier componentwise identical to a positive-chiral Majorana-Weyl spinor.

The same spin(11,3) Clifford presentation contains the Pati-Salam chain su(4)+su(2)_L+su(2)_R subset spin(10) subset spin(11,3), with the Standard Model generators as a subset and forty complementary spin(11,3) generators available for frame-Higgs roles.

L03 defines frame, spin connection, torsion, spin(10) Higgs covariant derivative, and combines spin connection, frame-Higgs, and gauge field into the spin(11,3) bosonic connection H=1/2 omega+1/4 e phi+A.

The curvature of the unified spin(11,3) bosonic connection decomposes into R-1/8 ee phi^2, mixed T phi-eDphi, and spin(10) gauge curvature sectors; the frame-Higgs vev is used to summarize symmetry breaking to gravity+SM and mass generation.

L03 represents boson-boson interactions by the spin(11,3) bivector Lie bracket and boson-fermion interactions by the chiral spinor action, then defines the fermion-fermion bracket trivially as zero to complete a semidirect Lie algebra with the spinor carrier as an ideal.
The conventional Standard Model algebra with its 64-real fermion carrier is likewise represented as a subalgebra of this GraviGUT semidirect algebra under the same bracket/action construction.

L03 constructs Cl(12,4) by extending the Cl(11,3) matrices, obtains 120 spin(12,4) bivectors with positive-chiral 128-real action, and uses 120 bivectors plus 128 positive-chiral spinor generators as the carrier decomposition of E8(-24).

The E8(-24) bracket differs structurally from the semidirect GraviGUT bracket: bivector-bivector and bivector-spinor brackets extend the spin action, while spinor-spinor brackets are nonzero and close back into the bivector sector via the spinor metric/Killing form.

L03 gives the E8(-24) Killing-form block structure, with spin(12,4) bivector signature (48,72), zero bivector-spinor pairing, spinor metric signature (64,64), and total signature (112,136), supporting the -24 real-form label.

The spin(11,3) GraviGUT embeds as the subalgebra generated by 91 selected spin(12,4) bivectors and 64 selected positive-chiral spinor generators, whose inherited bivector/action brackets exactly reproduce the GraviGUT brackets.

L03's exact algebraic embedding therefore includes both the gravity+SM Lie algebra and its correct action on one fermion generation; this exact embedding claim is distinct from any claim that every E8 generator has a physically correct particle interpretation.

A direct particle interpretation of all 248 E8(-24) generators predicts additional W'/Z', colored X bosons, a Peccei-Quinn-like w boson, extra frame-Higgs/axion roles, and a second 64-real block of mirror fermions with opposite charges.

L03 forms a superconnection A=H+psi from bosonic connection 1-forms and Grassmann-valued fermionic fields in the same algebra; its curvature contains F, Dpsi, and a quadratic psi psi term, with Dpsi matching the source's covariant Dirac derivative for the selected fermion subspace.

L04 treats a Dirac spinor as an irreducible representation of Pin(1,3), not merely Spin+(1,3), and distinguishes the Pin extension by parity P and unitary time conjugation T_U from the connected Lorentz-spin subgroup.

L04 represents Pin(1,3) inside the invertible Cl(1,3) elements, with Clifford reflections/adjoints giving the action on spinors and vectors; P and T_U anticommute and generate an order-8 finite subgroup.

L04 distinguishes Pin(1,3) from Pin(3,1) by the squares of P, T, and PT, then deliberately chooses the phase-modified representative U_P=i gamma_0 so spinors acquire P^2=-1 while calculations retain Spin+(1,3)≈SL(2,C).
